subject: science
name: Science
title: Kindergarten Science: Weather, Sunlight & Living Things
overview: Kindergarten Science fosters curiosity and scientific inquiry through hands-on experiments, outdoor observations, and interactive investigations aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS).
competencies: Ask testable questions and make systematic observations using sensory tools.
Investigate the interactions between physical forces, living organisms, and Earth's atmosphere.
Construct evidence-based explanations for everyday natural phenomena.
Design and evaluate simple solutions to environmental and everyday engineering challenges.

modules.title: Forces & Motion: Pushes and Pulls
modules.description: Investigating how pushes and pulls change the speed and direction of objects, and how collisions alter movement.

topics.title: Investigating Pushes and Pulls
topics.description: Testing how different strengths of pushes and pulls move toys across surfaces.

topics.title: Changing Direction & Collisions
topics.description: Observing how two moving objects affect each other upon collision.

modules.title: Sunlight, Warmth & Weather Patterns
modules.description: Exploring the warming effects of sunlight on Earth and tracking daily and seasonal weather changes.

topics.title: Sunlight & Thermal Warmth
topics.description: Measuring temperature differences in sunlight versus shade, and designing shade shelters.

topics.title: Weather Observations & Forecasting
topics.description: Recording local weather conditions (rain, snow, wind, sunshine) and preparing for severe weather.

modules.title: Plants, Animals & Environmental Stewardship
modules.description: Discovering what plants and animals need to survive and how humans can reduce their environmental footprint.

topics.title: Basic Needs of Living Things
topics.description: Investigating plant needs (light, water) and animal needs (food, water, shelter).

topics.title: Protecting Our Earth
topics.description: Exploring recycling, composting, saving water, and keeping local habitats clean.
